editorial_title_zh: 观点：超越指责：艺术市场修正期真正向我们索求的是什么
editorial_excerpt_zh: 画廊经营者帕斯卡尔·德·萨尔特（Pascal de Sarthe）反思了为什么当前艺术市场的周期性低迷与以往感觉有所不同。帕斯卡尔·德·萨尔特

article_text:
Issue

The Point: Beyond Blame: What the Art Market Correction Is Really Asking of Us

LAU WAI ’s “deSAR (DE SARTHE ARTIST RESIDENCY) X Lau Wai” at DE SARTHE, Hong Kong, 2026. Courtesy DE SARTHE.

I have been a dealer for nearly 50 years and have watched this argument arrive several times under different names. The art world keeps looking for someone to blame: first speculators, then fairs, before them the mega-galleries and the auction houses accused of turning art into a financial asset.

Let me say plainly what many people in this business think privately: much of what that system produced is decorative and commercial, and should never have been called art at all.

There is truth in these accusations, but the hunt leads nowhere. Blame asks who did this to us, a comfortable question because the answer is always someone else. The harder question is what kind of art world we intend to build now that the old one has run out of steam.

A correction is not a collapse, but an invitation to recalibrate. For decades the market’s energy went into velocity: how fast a name could rise, how many fairs a gallery could work, how quickly a work could be resold. That velocity produced excitement and opened doors for artists, but it crowded out something quieter and far more essential: the slow work of building a relationship between an artist, an idea, and the people who live with it.

A healthy market should optimize not for greed, vanity, or the next flip, but for the conversation a work makes possible with the person standing before it. Art is one of the few remaining spaces where a culture articulates itself to itself: what it values, what it fears, what it is still trying to understand. When the market drifts from that purpose, of course it corrects. The correction is not a punishment. It is the market remembering what it is for.
excerpt_original: Gallerist Pascal de Sarthe reflects on why the current art market’s cyclical downturn feels different from those that came before. Pascal de Sarthe

article_text:
Taylor Swift got some of the old gang back together for her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour, delivering a four-song set to a black-tie audience Saturday night at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala.

Conan O’Brien introduced her by saying, “It’s an insane, unprecedented honor to introduce a cherished member of our little ‘ Toy Story 5 ‘ family. She’s John, Paul, George and Ringo all in one.”

Related Stories

Christy Carlson Romano Says Her Salary Was Half of Shia LaBeouf's on 'Even Stevens': 'We Were Co-Leads and Had the Same Screen Time'

As an indicator of just how long she’s been off any kind of regular performance circuit, the gala-capping show included Swift’s first-ever live rendering of “ The Fate of Ophelia ,” the smash hit single she released just over a year ago, on Oct. 3, 2025. The song is expected to be a leading contender for record of the year and other categories at the 2027 Grammys, for which Recording Academy voters just received their first ballots.

Popular on Variety

🚨| Taylor Swift performing "The Fate of Ophelia" for the very first time at the Academy Museum Gala! pic.twitter.com/w1Pidc32mh — The Eras Tour (@tswifterastour) October 18, 2026

As expected, she also sang her contender for the 2027 Oscars, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Pixar film “Toy Story 5.” It wasn’t her first live performance ever of that song — she did it at the film premiere, at the Grammy Museum and at a private Ross House FYC showcase — but it was her first time singing it live with a full band. Besides its Oscar eligibility, the song is also in contention at the Grammys, entered in the song of the year category as well as film soundtrack and country divisions.

Taylor Swift performs “I Knew It, I Knew You” at the #AcademyMuseumGala pic.twitter.com/23reYW7dBU — Variety (@Variety) October 18, 2026

For the remaining two slots in her set, Swift dug farther back into the past, covering both her cynical and romantic bases, opening with “Blank Space” and ending with “Love Story.”

Wearing a Ralph Lauren gown for her performance, Swift invited the formally clad gathering to dance along with her set, saying, “Dancing is absolutely allowed. It’s not mandatory, but it’s more fun.”

Her backing crew had some singers and players who would be familiar to Swifties, but also some differences in the lineup, which was stripped down in some regards and packed out in others, namely with a horn section. She was joined by two sax players — not a regular staple of her touring outfit — as well as four singers and a guitarist, bassist, keyboard player and drummer.

Among the regular band members participating was Paul Sidoti, who wrote on Instagram, “Great to be playing music with my onstage partner of 19 years for the first time since The Eras Tour at a little party last night in Hollywood.”

Swift posed for photos with attendees including “Toy Story 5” voice actors Joan Cusack and Conan O’Brian and celebs like Cara Delevingne, Sabrina Carpenter, Eli Roth, Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo, John Carpenter, Hannah Waddingham, and Dakota and Elle Fanning.

Earlier in the night, Swift hit the red carpet wearing a pale blue Dior gown.

title_original: Photography at 200 through the Prix Pictet
editorial_title_zh: 透过百岁摄影奖（Prix Pictet）看摄影发展200年
editorial_excerpt_zh: 值此摄影术诞生二百周年之际，11位 Prix Pictet 奖得主展示了影像将我们带入塑造我们世界的环境与社会问题的不同方式。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "值此摄影术诞生二百周年之际，11位 Prix Pictet 奖得主展示了影像将我们带入塑造我们世界的环境与社会问题的不同方式。", "links": [{"text": "Prix Pictet", "url": "https://bit.ly/4zH9e8U"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在尼谢福尔·涅普斯（Nicéphore Niépce）拍下窗前风景的二百年后，除了相机取景框前的画面，一张照片还能揭示什么？在一个充斥着影像以及源源不断假新闻与虚假信息的时代，摄影师们又能做些什么来吸引我们的注意？艺术家们能否冲破这一切，帮助我们直面气候灾难这一紧迫挑战？环境破坏已被广泛拍摄，然而司空见惯可能会麻痹我们的反应。摄影是否仍具有带来变革的力量，或是将观众带入与其所描绘问题进行有意义对话的力量？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Prix Pictet 的11位得主为这些紧迫问题提供了不同的处理方法。该奖项由百达集团（Pictet Group）于2008年创立，旨在引起人们对可持续发展的关注，其认可的作品涵盖纪实观察、摆拍影像、合作肖像、热成像以及历史工艺。它连续的主题从“水”到“风暴”，将环境压力与产生并经历这些压力的社会联系起来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Benoit-Aquin-Untitled-01-2006.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Benoit Aquin", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首届获奖者、加拿大摄影师伯努瓦·阿坎（Benoit Aquin）通过荒漠化对生活在其中人们的影响，探讨了中国的荒漠化问题。他获奖的系列作品《中国的“尘暴区”》（The Chinese ‘Dust Bowl’）追溯了集约化耕作、过度放牧和水资源枯竭的后果。阿坎的照片记录了人们在因肥沃土壤流失而引发的沙尘暴中继续日常生活的情景。这些土壤随风飘散，成为空气污染，将后果扩散到该地区以外的更广阔地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纳达夫·坎德（Nadav Kander）的《长江》（Yangtze, The Long River，该奖项“地球”周期的得主）同样探讨了中国快速发展带来的环境与人类代价。这位总部位于伦敦的摄影师展示了在重塑河流景观、使既有社区流离失所的基础设施面前显得十分渺小的人们。在《重庆四号（周日野餐）》（Chongqing IV (Sunday Picnic)）中，大桥下的聚会赋予了这些变化一种人类尺度的衡量。这种对比提出了贯穿整个系列的问题：当经济进步依赖于社区和栖息地的破坏时，究竟失去了什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "米奇·爱泼斯坦（Mitch Epstein，该奖项“增长”周期的得主）将这种关系置于他自己的国家之内。他的系列作品《美国力量》（American Power）记录了美国民宅、道路和休闲空间中的能源生产，揭示了其基础设施如何全方位地塑造日常生活。这一标题也将我们的目光引向了决定这些景观的政治和企业利益。随后，爱泼斯坦与作家苏珊·贝尔（Susan Bell）合作，通过俄亥俄州的广告牌和一个网站将该项目进一步延伸，把相关问题带到了画廊之外。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/dSGNP.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Richard Mosse", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Luc-Delahaye-132nd-Ordinary-Meeting-of-the-Conference-OPEC-headquarters-Vienna-Austria-15-September-2004.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Luc Delahaye", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吕克·德拉艾（Luc Delahaye）曾是一名战地记者，后转向更为主观的创作方式，他审视了权力的行使方式以及权力塑造了谁的生活。这位法国摄影师的获奖作品集（针对“权力”周期）将政治和经济聚会与冲突和灾难纳入了相同的审视框架中。这些大型、细节丰富的照片吸引人们对这些事件中的人物给予持续关注，将政治和商业领袖做出的决策与其他人生活其中的不平等条件联系起来。它们将该奖项对可持续发展的关注延伸到了关于权威、不平等以及我们彼此责任的问题上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "迈克尔·施密特（Michael Schmidt）的《食品》（Lebensmittel）审视了我们所吃食物背后的工业系统。这位德国摄影师记录了农场、加工厂和包装产品，揭示了通常对消费者隐蔽的生产阶段。这些影像放在一起，对超市商品形态的食物与生产它所需的动物、土地和劳动力之间的距离提出了质疑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "理查德·莫斯（Richard Mosse）的《热力图》（Heat Maps）将强迫移民和流离失所者的待遇纳入了该奖项对可持续发展的考量中。这位爱尔兰艺术家使用军用热成像相机拍摄难民营和临时定居点，记录的是体温而非可见光。这种为监视而设计的设备将人们渲染为匿名的热源特征。他那令人不安的全景图提出了这样的问题：社会如何安顿那些寻求庇护的人，以及当弱势群体被当作需要监控的人口而非具有权利和需求的个体对待时，会发生什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Gauri-Gill-‘Jogiyon-ka-Dera-Lunkaransar-from-the-series-‘Notes-from-the-Desert.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Gauri Gill", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "美国摄影师莎莉·曼（Sally Mann）回溯了该媒介的过去。她的《黑水湿版摄影》（Blackwater tintypes）描绘了大迪斯莫尔沼泽（Great Dismal Swamp）——这里曾是逃离奴隶制的人们的避难所，也是后来因大面积火灾而伤痕累累的景观。照片暗沉、不安的表面暗示了将一个地方与其所承载的历史割裂开来的难度。一种19世纪的工艺变成了一种审视美国南方种族暴力挥之不去的方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "科特迪瓦艺术家乔安娜·舒马利（Joana Choumali）的《一切都会好起来的》（Ça va aller）探讨了人们如何从集体创伤中恢复过来。在大巴萨姆（Grand-Bassam）发生2016年恐怖袭击的三周后，她用iPhone拍摄了沉静的街道和孤独的身影，然后将彩色丝线直接绣在印刷品上。这种缓慢、重复的缝合成为她处理自身悲伤并应对那些常常无法言说之感的方式。该系列以“希望”为主题荣获该奖项，将一个社会的福祉与承认痛苦并寻找与之共存之道的艰难工作联系在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "印度摄影师高里·吉尔（Gauri Gill）的《来自沙漠的笔记》（Notes from the Desert）探讨了拉贾斯坦邦乡村的边缘化社群是如何维持生计的。该项目始于1999年，记录了干旱、贫困以及医疗和教育资源匮乏带来的压力，以及伴随这些压力的生老病死、劳作与庆祝。通过不断的走访与建立友谊，吉尔展现了生存如何依赖于人与人之间的关系以及自然环境。该系列作品以“人类”（Human）为主题被授予该奖项，将常被忽视的人们置于资源、不平等和集体福祉等核心问题的中心。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Valerie-Belin-Still-life-with-animals-2014.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Valérie Belin", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/1Ezr4.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Alfredo Jarr", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "瓦莱丽·贝兰（Valérie Belin）通过我们所获得的物品来探讨我们与资源的关系这位法国女摄影师的《静物》（Still Life）构图将廉价且主要是塑料的消费品带入了浮世绘般的传统之中，在这一传统中，财产成了对死亡的提醒。其光鲜亮丽的丰饶吸引着目光，而人体模型的碎片则暗示着人类的存在被物质的积累所淹没。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于出生于智利的艺术家、建筑师兼电影制作人阿尔弗雷多·贾尔（Alfredo Jaar）而言，对环境危机的回应采取了一种更为克制的形式。《终结》（The End）描绘了因过度引水而受到威胁的犹他州大盐湖。他选择以适中的尺寸冲印这些照片，将其描述为“视觉低语”。这种尺寸需要一种观看方式：观众必须走近才能直面正在消逝的壮丽。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本月，《终结》与贝兰的《静物》将在巴黎摄影展（Paris Photo）上展开对话，这也标志着百达集团（Pictet Group）与该展会建立新的官方合作伙伴关系。它们的并置——在大皇宫（Grand Palais）核心区域的漫步长廊（Promenoir）共同展出——将人工制造的丰裕与生态枯竭联系起来，利用静物和风景这两种熟悉的艺术体裁，让我们重新审视美的内涵。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "无论是关注还是理解都不能保证行动。然而，在这11种实践中，摄影创造了契机，让我们得以质疑我们所消费的物品、我们的生活方式以及哪些人的经历进入了公众视野。在走过两个世纪历史的今天，摄影依然能让熟悉的主题焕发新的视觉，促使我们重新思考我们以为自己已经理解的事物。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Prix Pictet将于2026年11月12日至15日在巴黎大皇宫（Grand Palais）的Promenoir展区呈现瓦莱丽·贝兰（Valérie Belin）与阿尔弗雷多·贾尔（Alfredo Jaar）的作品，预展于11月11日举行。", "links": [{"text": "Prix Pictet", "url": "https://bit.ly/4zH9e8U"}, {"text": "Paris Photo", "url": "https://bit.ly/4zH9e8U"}], "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "As photography marks its bicentenary, the 11 Prix Pictet laureates demonstrate the different ways an image can draw us into the environmental and social questions shaping our world.", "links": [{"text": "Prix Pictet", "url": "https://bit.ly/4zH9e8U"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Two hundred years after Nicéphore Niépce fixed the view from his window, what can a photograph reveal beyond the scene in front of the camera? And what can photographers do to get our attention in an age when we are deluged by images alongside a continuous flow of fake news and misinformation? Can artists cut through all this to help us face the urgent challenge of climate catastrophe? Environmental destruction is extensively photographed, yet familiarity can dull our response. Does photography retain the power to bring about change, or to bring audiences into meaningful dialogue with the issues it depicts?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The 11 laureates of the Prix Pictet offer different approaches to these pressing questions. Founded by the Pictet Group in 2008 to draw attention to sustainability, the prize has recognised work encompassing documentary observation, constructed images, collaborative portraiture, thermal imaging and historical processes. Its successive themes, from ‘Water’ to ‘Storm’, connect environmental pressures with the societies that produce and experience them."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Benoit-Aquin-Untitled-01-2006.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "©Benoit Aquin", "credit": "British Journal of Photography"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The inaugural winner, Canadian photographer Benoit Aquin, approached the issue of desertification in China through its effects on the people living with it. His winning series, The Chinese ‘Dust Bowl’ , traces the consequences of intensive cultivation, overgrazing and depleted water supplies. Aquin’s photographs show people going about their lives amid dust storms caused by the loss of fertile soil. Carried by the wind, that soil becomes airborne pollution, spreading the consequences far beyond the region."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nadav Kander’s Yangtze, The Long River (winner of the ‘Earth’ cycle) also considers the environmental and human costs of China’s rapid development. The London-based photographer shows people dwarfed by the infrastructure transforming the river landscape and displacing established communities. In Chongqing IV (Sunday Picnic) , a gathering beneath a vast bridge gives these changes a human measure. The contrast raises a question running through the series: what is lost when economic progress depends on the destruction of communities and habitats?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mitch Epstein (winner of the ‘Growth’ cycle) locates that relationship within his own country. article_text:
As photography marks its bicentenary, the 11 Prix Pictet laureates demonstrate the different ways an image can draw us into the environmental and social questions shaping our world.

Two hundred years after Nicéphore Niépce fixed the view from his window, what can a photograph reveal beyond the scene in front of the camera? And what can photographers do to get our attention in an age when we are deluged by images alongside a continuous flow of fake news and misinformation? Can artists cut through all this to help us face the urgent challenge of climate catastrophe? Environmental destruction is extensively photographed, yet familiarity can dull our response. Does photography retain the power to bring about change, or to bring audiences into meaningful dialogue with the issues it depicts?

The 11 laureates of the Prix Pictet offer different approaches to these pressing questions. Founded by the Pictet Group in 2008 to draw attention to sustainability, the prize has recognised work encompassing documentary observation, constructed images, collaborative portraiture, thermal imaging and historical processes. Its successive themes, from ‘Water’ to ‘Storm’, connect environmental pressures with the societies that produce and experience them.

The inaugural winner, Canadian photographer Benoit Aquin, approached the issue of desertification in China through its effects on the people living with it. His winning series, The Chinese ‘Dust Bowl’ , traces the consequences of intensive cultivation, overgrazing and depleted water supplies. Aquin’s photographs show people going about their lives amid dust storms caused by the loss of fertile soil. Carried by the wind, that soil becomes airborne pollution, spreading the consequences far beyond the region.

Nadav Kander’s Yangtze, The Long River (winner of the ‘Earth’ cycle) also considers the environmental and human costs of China’s rapid development. The London-based photographer shows people dwarfed by the infrastructure transforming the river landscape and displacing established communities. In Chongqing IV (Sunday Picnic) , a gathering beneath a vast bridge gives these changes a human measure. The contrast raises a question running through the series: what is lost when economic progress depends on the destruction of communities and habitats?

Mitch Epstein (winner of the ‘Growth’ cycle) locates that relationship within his own country. His series American Power captures energy production among homes, roads and recreational spaces in the US, revealing how thoroughly its infrastructure shapes everyday experience. The title also directs us towards the political and corporate interests determining these landscapes. With writer Susan Bell, Epstein subsequently extended the project through billboards in Ohio and a website, taking its questions beyond the gallery.

Luc Delahaye, a former war reporter who turned to a more subjective approach, examines how power is exercised and whose lives it shapes. The French photographer’s winning portfolio (for the ‘Power’ cycle) brings political and economic gatherings into the same frame of inquiry as conflict and disaster. The large, detailed photographs invite sustained attention to the people within these events, connecting decisions made by political and business leaders with the unequal conditions in which others live. They extend the prize’s concern with sustainability to questions of authority, inequality and our responsibility towards one another.

Michael Schmidt’s Lebensmittel examines the industrial systems behind the food we eat. The German photographer documented farms, processing plants and packaged products, revealing stages of production usually hidden from consumers. Seen together, the images question the distance between food as a supermarket commodity and the animals, land and labour required to produce it.

Richard Mosse’s Heat Maps brings forced migration and the treatment of displaced people into the prize’s consideration of sustainability. The Irish artist used a military thermal camera to photograph refugee camps and temporary settlements, recording body heat rather than visible light. Designed for surveillance, the equipment renders people as anonymous heat signatures. His unsettling panoramas ask how societies accommodate those seeking refuge, and what happens when vulnerable people are treated as populations to monitor rather than individuals with rights and needs.

American photographer Sally Mann reaches into the medium’s past. Her Blackwater tintypes depict the Great Dismal Swamp, a refuge for people escaping slavery and a landscape subsequently scarred by extensive fires. The photographs’ dark, troubled surfaces suggest the difficulty of separating a place from the histories it holds. A 19th-century process becomes a way to consider the persistence of racial violence within the American South.

Ivorian artist Joana Choumali’s Ça va aller considers how people recover from collective trauma. Three weeks after the 2016 terrorist attack in Grand-Bassam, she used her iPhone to photograph subdued streets and solitary figures, then embroidered colourful thread directly onto the prints. The slow, repetitive stitching became a way to process her own grief and address feelings that often went unspoken. Awarded the prize under the theme of ‘Hope’, the series connects the wellbeing of a community with the difficult work of acknowledging suffering and finding ways to live with it.

Indian photographer Gauri Gill’s Notes from the Desert explores how marginalised communities sustain their lives in rural Rajasthan. Begun in 1999, the project records births, deaths, work and celebrations alongside the pressures of drought, poverty and limited access to healthcare and education. Through repeated visits and friendships, Gill shows how survival depends on relationships with one another and the natural environment. Awarded the prize under the theme of ‘Human’, the series places people often overlooked at the centre of questions about resources, inequality and collective wellbeing.

Valérie Belin approaches our relationship with resources through the things we acquire. The Frenchwoman’s Still Life compositions bring cheap, predominantly plastic consumer objects into the vanitas tradition, in which possessions become reminders of mortality. Their glossy abundance attracts the eye, while mannequin fragments suggest a human presence overwhelmed by accumulation.

For Chilean-born artist, architect and filmmaker Alfredo Jaar, the response to the environmental crisis takes a more restrained form. The End depicts Utah’s Great Salt Lake, threatened by excessive water extraction. He chose to print the photographs at a modest size, describing them as a “visual whisper”. The scale requires an approach: viewers must move closer to encounter the immensity of what is being lost.

This month, The End and Belin’s Still Life will meet in conversation at Paris Photo, marking Pictet Group’s new official partnership with the fair. Their juxtaposition – exhibited together on the Promenoir at the heart of the Grand Palais – connects manufactured abundance with ecological depletion, using the familiar genres of still life and landscape to make us reconsider what beauty contains.

Neither attention nor understanding guarantees action. Across these 11 practices, however, photography creates occasions to question what we consume, how we live and whose experiences enter public view. Two centuries into its history, photography can still make familiar subjects newly visible, prompting us to reconsider what we thought we understood.

Prix Pictet presents Valérie Belin and Alfredo Jaar on the Promenoir at Paris Photo , Grand Palais, 12–15 November 2026, with a preview on 11 November.

article_text:
Veteran Indian actor Shabana Azmi and film critic and historian Marco Müller are among the guests at the first Kathmandu Film Festival (KFF), which runs Oct. 30–Nov. 1 in Nepal.

Launched by Kathmandu Metropolitan City, the three-day event will screen 40 films from 14 countries across several strands: the International Panorama, Nepal Panorama Shorts, a program of restored Nepali features and open-air screenings. Filmmakers and artists from around Asia are also due to attend. The city, a UNESCO Creative City of Film, set up the festival to showcase Nepali and international independent cinema and to build cultural ties.

Related Stories

Olivia Cooke on Returning to 'Slow Horses,' On-Set Injuries and That Shocking Finale Cliffhanger: 'I Want a Showdown!'

See-Saw Films Heads on Mediawan Sale, Why ‘Tenzing’ Was Their ‘Most Challenging’ Movie Yet and the ‘World Building’ Potential of ‘Slow Horses’ and ‘The NeverEnding Story’

Marine Atlan’s Cannes premiere “La Gradiva” is among the international selections, as is Shahrbanoo Sadat’s “No Good Men,” which debuted in Berlin this year.

“The international panorama is a curated showcase of global, contemporary and independent cinema that represents powerful stories, unique voices and distinct cultural perspectives,” said Ramyata Limbu, KFF’s artistic director. “The Nepal panorama shorts feature diverse and compelling stories about Nepal by emerging local talent.”

Nepal’s film history gets a section of its own. A retrospective of restored titles from the 1970s and 1980s includes “Kumari,” credited as the country’s first color feature.

Yamagata, Japan, which holds the same UNESCO film designation as Kathmandu, is the focus of a separate shorts program. Organizers tied the showcase to the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Nepal and Japan, and said it is meant to deepen links between the two cities.

Events are spread across venues including Basantapur, City Hall, the Nepal Tourism Board, Jai Nepal Cinema and Taragaon. Alongside the films, the lineup takes in a heritage walk, master classes and conversations with filmmakers, with prizes to be handed out in the youth video challenge and Nepal panorama sections. Screenings are free, though some events require booking ahead.

“Kathmandu is not just the city of its indigenous communities, whose culture and heritage are at its heart. It is also a city shaped by people from every corner of Nepal,” said Sunita Dangol, Kathmandu’s acting mayor. “Over generations, communities from across the country have brought their traditions, languages, art, music and stories to Kathmandu. That coming together is what makes this city so vibrant and unique.”

Organizers are pitching KFF as a festival for the general public, one that links the city’s heritage with present-day cinema and the global film community.

“Nepal has been through a profound tragedy with the floods, and in moments like these, stories become even more important,” Dangol said. “They help us make sense of what we have experienced, connect with one another, heal and find the courage to move forward.”

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在入选今年釜山国际电影节“开放电影”单元的泰国恐怖片《Inherit》中，一个古老的恶魔化身为迷人的超级名模。影片由欧莱雅代言人兼古驰品牌大使戴薇卡·霍内主演，饰演一个有着800年历史的蜈蚣恶魔，这是对一个广为人知的泰国故事进行的一次精致、诱惑且有趣的改编。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Inherit》不乏暴力和血腥场面，但让它脱颖而出的是其强烈的性感基调。作为恶魔沃娜纳（Woranart），霍内用她能想象到的最性感的服装，诱惑了视线所及的每一个人：男人、女人、男孩、女孩、亲戚、陌生人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "导演班庄·比辛达拿刚凭借《鬼影》（20004）等恐怖片热作建立了自己的声誉，但也执导过喜剧、爱情片以及泰国历史最高票房电影之一的《鬼夫》（2013）。他和霍内探讨了如何为现代审美品味改编一个熟悉的熟面孔故事、他们在涉及性与血腥时愿意走多远，以及如何在刀刺、斩首和虫杀等情节中紧紧抓住观众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们在他们的电影在釜山3000座露天剧场受到热烈欢迎后进行了采访。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Film Stage：你们能谈谈如何将古代传统与智能手机、购物中心等现代元素结合起来吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "班庄·比辛达拿刚：这是改编自泰国最著名的故事之一，即特里·阿披龙（Tri Aphirum）的小说《Tayard Asoon》（意为“恶魔的继承人”）。它已经被拍成过3个不同的电视剧版本。我记得30多年前看过第一版。当时觉得非常吓人，但现在我对它的印象已经变淡了。电脑特效可能有点过时了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是第一个故事片版本。我的直觉是，祖母沃娜纳必须显得非常现代。在故事开头，我有一个非常清晰的画面：她穿着比基尼在泳池边晒日光浴，手臂上有一个蜈蚣纹身。我想，“如果这个角色生活在现在、我们有手机、TikTok和这一切的时代，会怎么样呢？”我觉得这会使这个故事非常有趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个故事的每一个版本都有这样一个疯狂的场景——呕吐仪式。这已经成为了标志性桥段。我觉得凭借我们现在的电脑特效，它可以做得很好。我希望这部电影看起来有点像过去，但一切又发生在现在。所以我用老派恐怖片的方式拍摄它，使用了变焦镜头和过去的其他技巧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你是如何塑造沃娜纳这个角色的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "嗯，她是个恶魔对吧？但不能只有这一个层面。我们努力把她写得不那么吓人，她更有趣、带点疯狂。我们让她穿着奢华的衣服。每一套服装看起来都像是从时尚杂志里走出来的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她是你能想象到的最迷人的恶魔。在某种程度上有点像迪士尼的库伊拉（Cruella）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "实际上，我发给戴薇卡的参考对象是《本能》里的莎朗·石（Sharon Stone）。非常性感，但在她操纵片中每一个角色的方式上，也很有趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我很想知道动作戏的尺度可以推到多远。你们能展示的暴力类型有什么限制吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "没有真的限制。我觉得这一版应该非常疯狂，特别是在高潮部分。我希望沃娜纳彻底发狂。这与其他三个版本非常不同。而且我不想让它像我之前的恐怖片。这一部应该兼具：恐怖、动作、疯狂、搞笑，诸如此类。我把动作和血腥的极限推到了极致。鲜血会直接喷溅在你的脸庞上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Inherit》之所以如此成功，是因为你构建了一种包围式的、温室般的氛围。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如我所说，它不完全属于过去或现在。奥兰（Orlan）家族居住的房子的美术指导——大部分剧情都在那里发生——至关重要。这个家族非常富有，但我们选择了一栋老钱风的房子。它不是现代建筑，也不是现代家具。非常古老，就是那种能在墙上找到枪支和动物标本的房子。这让氛围更加挥之不去。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Banjong-PISANTHANAKUN-800x1200.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "班庄·比辛达拿刚", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你们是在实景地拍摄的吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大部分是的，但我们确实用了两个片场布景。奥兰家族的房子是由好几栋房子组合而成的。我想有两栋用于室内场景，大约三栋用于室外场景。街景和购物中心都是实景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他们允许你在购物中心里杀人？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们结合使用了两个购物中心。一个用于他们在顾客中穿行的镜头。当我们杀死扶梯上的那个男人时，我们用的是一个废弃的购物中心。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们尽量依靠真人特技而不是特效，尽管蜈蚣是用电脑制作的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "戴薇卡·霍内：你们在某个时刻看到的那个鬼魂就是我。那个老太婆。化那个妆花了7个小时，然后你只能看到她几秒钟。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "故事里的所有男人都很糟糕。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP：小说里就是这样。这是在对抗父权制。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH：所以奶奶做的是对的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们都继承了一个有缺陷的父权体制。但故事里的那些男人真的罪不至死吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP：这是他们的因果报应。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH：沃娜纳的背景故事是，800年前这个家族对她做了一件非常恶劣的事。大多数外国人不知道这个故事，但所有泰国人都知道。电影里有台词暗示了我和奶奶的遭遇，但从未确切解释。我们只知道我一代又一代、没完没了地纠缠着这个家族。我可没有去别的地方的打算。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "父亲是个工厂老板，剥削工人并通过毒素害死了许多人。大儿子是个恋童癖。甚至连男友塔特（Tat），他满脑子想的也只是跟女儿上床。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH：那是小年轻的事，他们就会那样。我只是盯着他们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他还是被揍得落花流水。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH：这也是我的计划的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP：因为继承人必须是处女。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "泰国观众已经知道那部分了吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "班庄·比辛达拿坤：没有，我们的结局是全新的。它和书里的不一样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：我本来应该“继承”她的妈妈，但我的姐姐帮她逃掉了。我消失了15年，然后又回来继承妈妈的女儿。为了做到这一点，我必须等她来月经，然后把我的蜈蚣吐进她体内。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你的第一个受害者做了什么，才落得如此可怕的下场？她深夜喝完酒走在街上，而你强行把她的脸按进油炸锅里。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：我只是路过，觉得饿了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你更喜欢演好人还是坏人？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：都喜欢。能演这个角色我很幸运。当你高高在上、俯视那些任你玩弄心思的人时，那种感觉很有趣。平时我总是那个听话、被动的人。偶尔演一次这样的角色很有意思，特别是泰国的这类角色并不多。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你穿了多少套衣服？十多套之后我就数不清了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：衣服太多了。你知道那件金色的吗？我和古驰有合作，他们很好心地为奶奶送来了那条裙子。它价值大约300万泰铢[9万美元]。这些服装对我们塑造角色很有帮助。很多服装灵感都来自班庄和造型师。实际上，所有角色的造型都来自班庄。他很有时尚感。他清楚地知道自己想让奶奶呈现什么造型。电影里有几套标志性的服装。我想今年万圣节你们就可以打扮成我的样子了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Inherit-1-1-1200x800.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "还有从哪个电影角色身上汲取过灵感吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：班庄发给我很多参考资料。我得挑出能用的部分。其中一个是《沉默的羔羊》里的汉尼拔·莱克特，他在操纵他人方面很有手段。另外，蜈蚣其实是个男人，所以我必须学习当一个女孩走进房间时，男人是怎么用眼神看的。莱克特是通过保持静止来做到这一点的，但我们的目光却无法从他身上移开。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了恐怖片，你还想涉足其他类型的电影吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "班庄·比辛达拿坤：我拍过爱情喜剧、家庭喜剧、恐怖喜剧。《鬼夫》是我最大的电影之一，是一部喜剧。《你好，陌生人》是一部爱情片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内，你在寻找什么样的角色？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黛维卡·霍内：我喜欢冒险。在我的上一部作品里，我演了一个吸尘器（《A Useful Ghost》）。我选择工作的方式不只是看项目本身，还要看环境和人。导演、编剧、所有的剧组人员。首要的是剧本。如果你问我喜欢什么类型，没有特别指定的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "能具体剖析一个场景吗？你让小儿子朗讪去房子底下收集用来对付沃拉纳特的泥土。一具尸体从泥土里爬出来袭击了他。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "班庄·比辛达拿坤：我们在片场花了一天时间拍那场戏。我们先画了分镜头脚本。上面看到的地下室天花板是我们后来用CGI加上去的，这样我们就能把摄像机架好拍俯拍镜头。我们请了一位杂技演员来演尸体，这样才能拍出他那些怪异的动作。我想我们大概拍了10条。这一切都是为了最后那个惊吓。外面的观众对那一幕反响非常热烈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《继承》在2026年釜山国际电影节上进行了展映。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "An ancient demon takes the form of a glamorous supermodel in Inherit , a Thai horror film that screened in the Open Cinema section of this year’s Busan International Film Festival. Starring Davika Hoorne, a spokesperson for L’Oréal and brand ambassador for Gucci, as an 800-year-old centipede demon, the movie is a polished, seductive, and funny version of a well-known Thai story."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Inherit has its share of violence and gore, but what sets it apart is its intensely sexual tone. As the demon Woranart, Hoorne seduces everyone in sight: men, women, boys, girls, relatives, strangers, all while dressed in the slinkiest outfits imaginable."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Director Banjong Pisanthanakun made his reputation with horror hits like Shutter (20004), but has also helmed comedies, romances, and Pee Mak (2013), one of Thailand’s highest-grossing films. He and Horne talked about adapting a familiar story for modern tastes, about how far they were willing to go in terms of sex and gore, and about holding onto an audience through knifings, decapitations, and death-by-insect."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We spoke after their film received a rousing reception at Busan’s 3000-seat outdoor theater."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Film Stage: Can you talk about combining ancient traditions with modern elements like smartphones and shopping malls?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Banjong Pisanthanakun: This is adapted from one of the most well-known stories in Thailand, a novel called Tayard Asoon (“The Demon’s Heir”) by Tri Aphirum. It’s already been made into three different TV series. I remember watching the first version more than 30 years ago. It was very scary, but my impressions of it now are faded. The CGI is maybe a bit outdated."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This is the first feature film version. What I felt was that the grandmother, Woranart, has to appear to be very modern. I had a very clear vision of her wearing a bikini, sunbathing by the pool in the beginning of the story, with a centipede tattoo on her arm. I wondered, “What if this character is living now, when we have cell phones and TikTok and everything?” I thought that would make the story really fun."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Every single version of the story has this crazy scene, a vomit ritual. It’s become iconic. I felt with the CGI we have now it could be great. I wanted the movie to look a bit like the past, but with everything taking place in the present. So I shot it like an old-time horror film, using zoom lenses and other techniques from the past."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "How did you develop Woranart’s character?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Well, she’s a demon, right? But that can’t be the whole story. We tried to write her so she wasn’t that scary, she’s more fun, a little crazy. We have her dressing in lavish clothes. Every outfit looks like it came out of a fashion catalogue."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "She’s the most seductive demon imaginable. In a way a little like Disney’s Cruella."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Actually, the reference that I sent Davika was Sharon Stone in Basic Instinct . Very sexy, but funny, too, in the way she manipulates every single character in the film."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I’m curious how far you can take the action. Do you have restrictions on the kind of violence you can show?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Not really. I felt this version should be really crazy, especially at the climax. I wanted Woranart to be totally nuts. Very different from the other three versions. And I didn’t want it to be like my previous horror films. This one should go: horror, action, crazy, funny, something like that. I pushed the limits of action and gore. Blood will be splattering in your face."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Inherit works so well because you build an enveloping, hot-house atmosphere."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As I said, it’s not in the past or the present. The art direction of the house where the Orlan family lives, where most of the action takes place, was crucial. The family’s very wealthy, but we chose an old-money house. It’s not modern architecture, modern furniture. Very old, the type of house where you find guns and mounted trophies on the walls. That made the atmosphere more haunting."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Banjong-PISANTHANAKUN-800x1200.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Banjong Pisanthanakun"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Did you shoot on actual locations?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mostly yes, but we did have two studio sets. The Orlan family house was a combination of several houses. Two for indoor scenes, I think three for scenes outside the house. The street scenes were locations, and the shopping mall."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "They let you kill people in the shopping mall?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We used a mix of two malls. One for when they’re walking among customers. When we kill the man on the escalator, we used an abandoned mall."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We tried to rely on practical stunts rather than effects, although the centipedes were CGI."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Davika Hoorne: The ghost you see at one point is me. That old hag. It took seven hours to apply the makeup, and then you only see her for a few seconds."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "All the men in the story are terrible."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: That’s in the novel. It’s against the patriarchy."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: So Grandma does the right thing."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We all inherit a flawed patriarchal system. But do the men in the story deserve to die?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: It’s their karma."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: Woranart’s backstory is that 800 years ago this family did something really bad to her. Most foreigners don’t know that story, but all Thais know it. There’s dialogue in the film that hints about what happened to me, the grandma, but it’s never explained exactly. All we know is that I keep haunting the family over and over again, for generations. I don’t have any plans to go anywhere else."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The father, a factory owner, exploited his workers and killed many of them through toxins. The eldest son is a pedophile. Even Tat, the boyfriend, all he’s trying to do is have sex with the daughter."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: That’s teenager stuff, that’s what they do. I just keep an eye on them."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He still gets beaten to a pulp."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: That is part of my plan, too."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: Because the inheritor has to be a virgin."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Thai audience already knows that part?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: No, our ending is new. It’s not the same as the one in the book."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: I was supposed to “inherit” her mom, but my sister helped her get away. I disappear for 15 years, then come back to inherit the mother’s daughter. To do that, I have to wait for her menses and then vomit my centipede into her."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What did your first victim do to deserve her grisly death? She’s walking down a street after a night of drinking, and you force her to dunk her face into a deep fryer."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: I was just passing by and felt hungry."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Do you prefer playing good or evil?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: Both. I’m blessed playing this character. It’s fun when you sit on top and look down on all the people whose minds you will be playing with. Normally I’m the one who always obeys, someone passive. It’s fun doing this character once in a while, especially because there aren’t many roles like this in Thailand."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "How many outfits do you wear? I lost count after a dozen."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: So many outfits. You know the gold one? I work with Gucci, and they were kind enough to send that dress for grandma. It cost some three million baht [$90,000]. The outfits help us a lot to create the character. A lot of the inspiration for the outfits came from Banjong, and the stylist. Actually, all the characters’ looks came from Banjong. He’s very fashionable. He knew exactly the look he wanted for Grandma. There are a few iconic outfits in the movie. I think this Halloween you will be able to dress as me."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Inherit-1-1-1200x800.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Was there another film character you drew inspiration from?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: Banjong sent me a lot of references. I had to pick and choose what to use. One was Hannibal Lecter in Silence of the Lambs , in the way he manipulated people. Also, the centipede is actually a man, so I had to learn how a man uses his eyes when a girl comes into the room. Lecter does it by remaining still, but we can’t take our eyes off him."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Would you like to work in other genres besides horror?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: I’ve done romcoms, I’ve done domestic comedies, horror comedies. Pee Mak , one of my biggest films, was a comedy. Hello Stranger was a romance."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Davika, what kinds of roles are you looking for?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "DH: I like to take risks. In my last project I played a vacuum cleaner ( A Useful Ghost ). The way I choose to work, it’s not just about the project. It’s about the environment and the people. The director, screenwriter, all the crew. The first thing is the script. If you ask me about genre, there’s nothing specific."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Can you break down a scene? You send the young son Rangsan under the house to gather soil that will be used in a spell against Woratan. A corpse crawls out of the dirt to attack him."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BP: We shot that in a day in the studio. We storyboarded it first. The basement ceiling above we added later with CGI, so we could position the camera for an overhead shot. We hired an acrobat to play the corpse, so we could film those weird moves he makes. I think we did about ten takes. It all builds up to that jump scare. article_text:
An ancient demon takes the form of a glamorous supermodel in Inherit , a Thai horror film that screened in the Open Cinema section of this year’s Busan International Film Festival. Starring Davika Hoorne, a spokesperson for L’Oréal and brand ambassador for Gucci, as an 800-year-old centipede demon, the movie is a polished, seductive, and funny version of a well-known Thai story.

Inherit has its share of violence and gore, but what sets it apart is its intensely sexual tone. As the demon Woranart, Hoorne seduces everyone in sight: men, women, boys, girls, relatives, strangers, all while dressed in the slinkiest outfits imaginable.

Director Banjong Pisanthanakun made his reputation with horror hits like Shutter (20004), but has also helmed comedies, romances, and Pee Mak (2013), one of Thailand’s highest-grossing films. He and Horne talked about adapting a familiar story for modern tastes, about how far they were willing to go in terms of sex and gore, and about holding onto an audience through knifings, decapitations, and death-by-insect.

We spoke after their film received a rousing reception at Busan’s 3000-seat outdoor theater.

The Film Stage: Can you talk about combining ancient traditions with modern elements like smartphones and shopping malls?

Banjong Pisanthanakun: This is adapted from one of the most well-known stories in Thailand, a novel called Tayard Asoon (“The Demon’s Heir”) by Tri Aphirum. It’s already been made into three different TV series. I remember watching the first version more than 30 years ago. It was very scary, but my impressions of it now are faded. The CGI is maybe a bit outdated.

This is the first feature film version. What I felt was that the grandmother, Woranart, has to appear to be very modern. I had a very clear vision of her wearing a bikini, sunbathing by the pool in the beginning of the story, with a centipede tattoo on her arm. I wondered, “What if this character is living now, when we have cell phones and TikTok and everything?” I thought that would make the story really fun.

Every single version of the story has this crazy scene, a vomit ritual. It’s become iconic. I felt with the CGI we have now it could be great. I wanted the movie to look a bit like the past, but with everything taking place in the present. So I shot it like an old-time horror film, using zoom lenses and other techniques from the past.

How did you develop Woranart’s character?

Well, she’s a demon, right? But that can’t be the whole story. We tried to write her so she wasn’t that scary, she’s more fun, a little crazy. We have her dressing in lavish clothes. Every outfit looks like it came out of a fashion catalogue.

She’s the most seductive demon imaginable. In a way a little like Disney’s Cruella.

Actually, the reference that I sent Davika was Sharon Stone in Basic Instinct . Very sexy, but funny, too, in the way she manipulates every single character in the film.

I’m curious how far you can take the action. Do you have restrictions on the kind of violence you can show?

Not really. I felt this version should be really crazy, especially at the climax. I wanted Woranart to be totally nuts. Very different from the other three versions. And I didn’t want it to be like my previous horror films. This one should go: horror, action, crazy, funny, something like that. I pushed the limits of action and gore. Blood will be splattering in your face.

Inherit works so well because you build an enveloping, hot-house atmosphere.

As I said, it’s not in the past or the present. The art direction of the house where the Orlan family lives, where most of the action takes place, was crucial. The family’s very wealthy, but we chose an old-money house. It’s not modern architecture, modern furniture. Very old, the type of house where you find guns and mounted trophies on the walls. That made the atmosphere more haunting.

Banjong Pisanthanakun

Did you shoot on actual locations?

Mostly yes, but we did have two studio sets. The Orlan family house was a combination of several houses. Two for indoor scenes, I think three for scenes outside the house. The street scenes were locations, and the shopping mall.

They let you kill people in the shopping mall?

We used a mix of two malls. One for when they’re walking among customers. When we kill the man on the escalator, we used an abandoned mall.

We tried to rely on practical stunts rather than effects, although the centipedes were CGI.

Davika Hoorne: The ghost you see at one point is me. That old hag. It took seven hours to apply the makeup, and then you only see her for a few seconds.

All the men in the story are terrible.

BP: That’s in the novel. It’s against the patriarchy.

DH: So Grandma does the right thing.

We all inherit a flawed patriarchal system. But do the men in the story deserve to die?

BP: It’s their karma.

DH: Woranart’s backstory is that 800 years ago this family did something really bad to her. Most foreigners don’t know that story, but all Thais know it. There’s dialogue in the film that hints about what happened to me, the grandma, but it’s never explained exactly. All we know is that I keep haunting the family over and over again, for generations. I don’t have any plans to go anywhere else.

The father, a factory owner, exploited his workers and killed many of them through toxins. The eldest son is a pedophile. Even Tat, the boyfriend, all he’s trying to do is have sex with the daughter.

DH: That’s teenager stuff, that’s what they do. I just keep an eye on them.

He still gets beaten to a pulp.

DH: That is part of my plan, too.

BP: Because the inheritor has to be a virgin.

The Thai audience already knows that part?

BP: No, our ending is new. It’s not the same as the one in the book.

DH: I was supposed to “inherit” her mom, but my sister helped her get away. I disappear for 15 years, then come back to inherit the mother’s daughter. To do that, I have to wait for her menses and then vomit my centipede into her.

What did your first victim do to deserve her grisly death? She’s walking down a street after a night of drinking, and you force her to dunk her face into a deep fryer.

DH: I was just passing by and felt hungry.

Do you prefer playing good or evil?

DH: Both. I’m blessed playing this character. It’s fun when you sit on top and look down on all the people whose minds you will be playing with. Normally I’m the one who always obeys, someone passive. It’s fun doing this character once in a while, especially because there aren’t many roles like this in Thailand.

How many outfits do you wear? I lost count after a dozen.

DH: So many outfits. You know the gold one? I work with Gucci, and they were kind enough to send that dress for grandma. It cost some three million baht [$90,000]. The outfits help us a lot to create the character. A lot of the inspiration for the outfits came from Banjong, and the stylist. Actually, all the characters’ looks came from Banjong. He’s very fashionable. He knew exactly the look he wanted for Grandma. There are a few iconic outfits in the movie. I think this Halloween you will be able to dress as me.

Was there another film character you drew inspiration from?

DH: Banjong sent me a lot of references. I had to pick and choose what to use. One was Hannibal Lecter in Silence of the Lambs , in the way he manipulated people. Also, the centipede is actually a man, so I had to learn how a man uses his eyes when a girl comes into the room. Lecter does it by remaining still, but we can’t take our eyes off him.

Would you like to work in other genres besides horror?

BP: I’ve done romcoms, I’ve done domestic comedies, horror comedies. Pee Mak , one of my biggest films, was a comedy. Hello Stranger was a romance.

Davika, what kinds of roles are you looking for?

DH: I like to take risks. In my last project I played a vacuum cleaner ( A Useful Ghost ). The way I choose to work, it’s not just about the project. It’s about the environment and the people. The director, screenwriter, all the crew. The first thing is the script. If you ask me about genre, there’s nothing specific.

Can you break down a scene? You send the young son Rangsan under the house to gather soil that will be used in a spell against Woratan. A corpse crawls out of the dirt to attack him.

BP: We shot that in a day in the studio. We storyboarded it first. The basement ceiling above we added later with CGI, so we could position the camera for an overhead shot. We hired an acrobat to play the corpse, so we could film those weird moves he makes. I think we did about ten takes. It all builds up to that jump scare. The audience outside really responded to that moment.

Inherit screened at the 2026 Busan International Film Festival.

Bowman），在出任匹兹堡大学第十任校长后，并没有把西宾夕法尼亚州起伏的山峦和崎岖的山谷视为理所当然。这或许可以解释，他如何能将这座城市视作美国高等教育史上最宏大、最激进的项目之一的选址。正如《纽约时报》两个月后所报道的那样，1924年11月，鲍曼在典雅的大学俱乐部（University Club）汇集了一百多位商业领袖以及“并不好对付的董事会”，公布了他那项雄心勃勃的计划：在匹大日益扩大的校园中心建造一座52层的哥特复兴风格学术摩天大楼。", "links": [{"text": "put it", "url": "https://www.nytimes.com/1924/11/30/archives/skyscraper-university-plan-is-unfolded-chancellor-bowman-sets-forth.html?ref=hyperallergic.com"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当时，奥克兰（Oakland）社区刚被开发为一个文化中心。它包括卡内基研究所的博物馆；匹兹堡交响乐团首次演出的卡内基音乐厅；圣保罗大教堂的新教区所在地；意大利风格的匹兹堡运动协会；共和国大军的学院派风格士兵与水手纪念碑（以哈利卡纳索斯陵墓为原型）；当然，还有海盗队打球的福布斯球场。如今，这位曾任艾奥瓦州单房间学校的教师设想在阿勒格尼县几乎精确的地理中心，竖起一座名副其实的教育理念纪念碑。建筑师查尔斯·泽勒·克劳德（Charles Zeller Klauder）的一位同僚为其取了个绰号叫“学习大教堂”（Cathedral of Learning），这个称呼和建筑本身一样荒诞而辉煌，并正式流传了下来。今天看来，对高等教育进行如此富有远见的投资——而且并非完全是为了颂扬那些名字并未装饰在建筑上的企业赞助商，而是为了灌输鲍曼所说的“惊叹”——几乎带有乌托邦色彩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/2026/10/image-22.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "维基共享资源）", "links": [{"text": "Wikimedia Commons", "url": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CathoLearn.jpg?ref=hyperallergic.com"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从大学俱乐部的宴会厅放眼望去，鲍曼当时可能指着由银行家兼受托人安德鲁·W·梅隆（Andrew W. Mellon）——当时任财政部长、后来成为华盛顿特区国家美术馆创立者——最近购得的空地，称这将是他建造世界上最伟大学术建筑的地址。鲍曼的前任们曾希望匹大的校园能成为沿着山坡蜿蜒而上的某种当代卫城，但到目前为止，现实中仅包含少数几栋新古典主义建筑和第一次世界大战期间建造的临时建筑。在纽约和芝加哥驻留期间，鲍曼逐渐认识到未来是垂直的而非水平的，因此他设想将学院的功能与摩天大楼的形式融合在一起，尽管这是一座不同寻常的大楼，他曾对《纽约时报》的记者说，从“古代开始……人类最伟大的纪念碑都直指天空”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "就在今年一个世纪前动工时，学习大教堂本将成为世界上第三高的摩天大楼。当它于1937年完工时，它是地球上最高的教育结构（并且仍然是西半球最高的一座）。据传说，一贯亲力亲为的鲍曼在试图与克劳德共同构思其愿景时，后者在播放理查德·瓦格纳的《女武神》中的“魔幻火之乐”时终于灵感迸发。两人深受启发，决定建造一座体现约翰·拉斯金在《威尼斯之石》（1851）中所论述观点的塔楼，即只有在哥特式建筑流派中，人们才能找到让“充满瑕疵的碎片升华为宏伟且无可指责的整体”的方法。正如鲍曼对前述《纽约时报》采访者所言：“难道我们不该认真对待这样一个观点：美如同真理一样对生命至关重要？”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于已经与学习大教堂共存了一个世纪（如果算其实际面貌则略短一些）的匹兹堡人来说，这座熟悉的印第安纳石灰岩雪花石膏城堡——它曾因创造了建造此类纪念碑所需财富的钢铁厂那无休止的烟雾而被熏黑——很容易因其奇异的壮丽而被忽视。高达42层（因股市崩盘向经济现实妥协而缩减了高度），占地面积超过50万平方英尺，并配备了12部电梯，这座大教堂如同一尊魔像般耸立在奥克兰上空。今天，它不仅不是世界第三高建筑，而且在匹兹堡仅排第八高，然而这座大教堂依然遗世独立。尽管奥克兰的天际线在过去的一个世纪里有所增长，但建筑历史学家马丁·奥兰德（Martin Aurand）对我说，从美学上讲，这座大教堂“保留了其建筑特色，因为它主导了其城市环境……它坐落在一片草地上，与其他建筑保持距离，并在邻近建筑之上高高耸立”，这与其它城市中高度相似的摩天大楼不同。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Feature

The Cathedral of Learning Is Pittsburgh’s Secular Temple

This year marks the centennial of one of the most audacious projects in the history of American higher education.

Carnegie Museum of Art )

A son of the Iowa prairies, John G. Bowman didn’t take the dramatic hills and rugged valleys of western Pennsylvania for granted after he became the tenth chancellor of the University of Pittsburgh. This may explain how he was able to view the city as a site for one of the most audacious projects in the history of American higher education. Gathering over a hundred business leaders alongside “no easy board of trustees” at the elegant University Club in November of 1924, as the New York Times put it two months later, Bowman unveiled his audacious plan to construct a 52-story neo-Gothic academic skyscraper at the center of Pitt’s growing campus.

At that time, the Oakland neighborhood had newly been developed into a cultural hub. It included the museums of the Carnegie Institute; the Carnegie Music Hall, where the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra first performed; the new diocesan seat of Saint Paul’s Cathedral; the Italianate Pittsburgh Athletic Association; the Grand Army of the Republic’s Beaux-Arts Soldiers and Sailors Memorial (modeled after the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus); and, of course, Forbes Field, where the Pirates played. Now, the former one-room schoolteacher from Iowa envisioned placing, at the almost exact geographical center of Allegheny County, a veritable monument to the idea of education. An associate of architect Charles Zeller Klauder nicknamed it the “Cathedral of Learning,” an appellation as preposterous and glorious as the building itself, which officially stuck. That such a visionary investment in higher education was once possible — and not entirely for the purpose of aggrandizing corporate sponsors, whose names don’t adorn the building, but rather to inculcate “wonder,” as Bowman put it — seems virtually utopian today.

Wikimedia Commons )

Looking out from the University Club’s ballroom, Bowman would have gestured to the empty field recently purchased by banker and trustee Andrew W. Mellon — then the Secretary of the Treasury and later the founder of Washington, DC’s National Gallery of Art — as being the site on which he would construct the greatest academic building in the world. Bowman’s predecessors had wanted Pitt’s campus to be a kind of contemporary Acropolis snaking up the hillside, but so far, the reality only included a handful of neo-classical buildings and temporary structures built during the First World War. After stints in both New York and Chicago, where Bowman came to understand that the future was vertical rather than horizontal, he envisioned fusing the function of the college with the form of a skyscraper, albeit an unusual one, telling the Times reporter that from “times of antiquity … man’s greatest monuments have pointed to the sky.”

When the ground was broken a century ago this year, the Cathedral of Learning would have been the third-tallest skyscraper in the world. When it was completed in 1937, it was the tallest educational structure on earth (and remains the tallest in the Western Hemisphere). According to the legend, when the ever-involved Bowman was trying to conceptualize his vision with Klauder, the latter was finally struck by inspiration when he put on Richard Wagner’s “Magic Fire Music” from Die Walküre . The two were inspired to construct a tower embodying John Ruskin’s argument from The Stones of Venice (1851) that only in the Gothic schools of architecture does one find a way for “fragments full of imperfection [to] raise up a stately and unaccusable whole.” As Bowman put it to the aforementioned interviewer for the New York Times: “Isn’t it time that we should take seriously the idea that beauty is essential to life as truth?”

For Pittsburghers, who’ve lived with the idea of the Cathedral of Learning for a century now (if its reality for a little less), the familiar alabaster castle of Indiana limestone — which was once stained black with the relentless smog of the steel mills that created the wealth that made the construction of such monuments possible — can be easily overlooked for its strange magnificence. Forty-two stories tall (the shortened height a concession to economic reality, after the stock market crashed), encompassing more than half a million square feet and equipped with 12 elevators, the Cathedral looms golem-like over Oakland. Today, it’s not only not the third-tallest building in the world, but only the eighth tallest in Pittsburgh, yet the Cathedral still stands alone. While the Oakland skyline has grown over the intervening century, architectural historian Martin Aurand told me that aesthetically, the Cathedral “retains its architectural distinction because it dominates its urban setting …. It stands free of other buildings on a grassy plot of land, and it towers above its neighbors,” unlike similarly high skyscrapers in other cities.
excerpt_original: This year marks the centennial of one of the most audacious projects in the history of American higher education.

article_text:
Announcement

UCLA’s MFA in Media Arts Now Accepting Applications

A three-year program for artists critically and experimentally engaging with media, technology, and contemporary culture.

DMA MFA Alumni Chelly Jin’s thesis installation, CHOREOCODEX v5.1.0

The MFA in Media Arts at UCLA is a three-year program for artists working critically and experimentally with media, technology, and contemporary culture. Through studio practice, technical and theoretical seminars, group critiques, and individual tutorials with faculty, students develop ambitious bodies of work while questioning established ideas about art, technology, and what it means to be a media artist today.

Located in Los Angeles within UCLA’s School of the Arts and Architecture, the program combines the intimacy of a small graduate cohort with the resources of a major research university. Students work closely with faculty whose practices span computational and generative art, moving image, performance, games, sound, design, critical media studies, AI, networked culture, and experimental forms of publishing and research.

Students have access to financial aid, paid teaching and research assistantships, grants, and fellowships, as well as 24-hour access to the department’s shop and digital fabrication facilities. Research and creative communities include the UCLA Game Lab , UCLA Social Software , Art|Sci Center , CounterForce Lab , and UCLA Arts Conditional Studio .

Faculty include Steve Anderson, Jenna Caravello, Erkki Huhtamo, Peter Lunenfeld, Lauren McCarthy, Chandler McWilliams, Rebeca Méndez, Romi Morrison, Sahej Rahal, Casey Reas, Mindy Seu, Danny Snelson, Ramesh Srinivasan, and Eddo Stern. Students are also encouraged to work across UCLA, drawing on courses, research, and communities throughout the university.

We welcome applicants from a wide range of backgrounds, disciplines, and forms of practice, particularly those whose work expands what media art can be.

The application deadline is January 4, 2027.

To learn more about the program or register for a virtual information session, visit mfa.dma.ucla.edu .

title_original: A Talent for Murder review – Helen Mirren is a viperous Patricia Highsmith in hit-and-miss thriller
editorial_title_zh: 《天才谋杀》影评——海伦·米伦在一部有失水准的惊悚片中饰演满嘴刻薄的帕特ري西亚·海史密斯
editorial_excerpt_zh: 多伦多电影节：这部对暴躁犯罪作家进行虚构创作的影片讲述了她与一位雄心勃勃的编辑共同策划一场谋杀的故事，但剧本亟需更多锋芒。疫情的限制不可避免地带来了对安全封闭式室内剧电影的推崇，这类影片中少数几位……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "疫情带来的限制不可避免地推动了安全封闭的室内剧（chamber-piece）电影的兴起，少数角色往往聚集在一处偏僻的房子里，对话明显压倒了动作。其中有一些亮点，比如凯文·威廉姆森（Kevin Williamson）切合时宜的惊悚片《身同感受》（Sick），也有相当糟糕的低谷，比如萨姆·莱文森（Sam Levinson）空洞的剧情片《马尔科姆与玛丽》（Malcolm & Marie）。不过，尽管我们看了不少这类作品，却没有一部能与大流行前那些最伟大、最聪明的同类作品相媲美。最好的作品往往改编自话剧，而且主演通常是迈克尔·凯恩（Michael Caine）。", "links": [{"text": "Covid", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/coronavirus-outbreak"}, {"text": "Sick", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/jan/12/sick-review-covid-kevin-willianson-scream"}, {"text": "Malcolm & Marie", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/jan/22/malcolm-marie-review-sam-levinson-with-zendaya-john-david-washington"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他曾出演安东尼·谢弗（Anthony Shaffer）的《侦探》（Sleuth），该片在1970年代从托尼奖走向了奥斯卡，并在随后的十年里出演了可以说是更好的《死亡陷阱》（Deathtrap）——西德尼·吕美特（Sidney Lumet）将伊拉·莱文（Ira Levin）构思巧妙的话剧改编成了这部电影。在这期间，还有一部鲜为人知的电视电影《我的一个妻子失踪了》（One of My Wives Is Missing），改编自60年代的话剧《单身汉陷阱》（Trap for a Single Man），虽然明显逊色，但依然带来了同样独特的曲折、对白驱动的惊悚快感。其中会有秘密、惊喜、反转，而且到最后通常至少有一具尸体，这是一个完全归功于阿加莎·克里斯蒂（Agatha Christie）作品的子类型（据报道，她非常喜欢舞台版的《侦探》，甚至亲笔签名了一张照片挂在大银幕改编版所用的房子里）。因此，这一标准的门槛相当高，这是一个需要极高明剧作水平的谜题，既要聪明而不自鸣得意，又要震撼而不显得廉价。", "links": [{"text": "One of My Wives Is Missing", "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7V3WtoRxRtQ&"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《天才谋杀》（A Talent for Murder）是一次令人钦佩且罕见的尝试，试图将这种模式重新带回，这是一次险些成功的大胆尝试。它同样改编自一部话剧，并且像《侦探》和《死亡陷阱》一样，围绕着一位作家展开，她用自己编织的方式穿梭于自己一手打造的惊悚片情节中。接替凯恩的是海伦·米伦（Helen Mirren），她饰演的是帕特里西亚·海史密斯（Patricia Highsmith）的一个虚构版本——这位作家以暴躁和偏执闻名，讨厌与人交往，而且像大多数厌世者一样，她更喜欢动物。我们于1995年在瑞士的一处偏僻住宅里见到她，当时她正借酒浇愁，不再写作，只有一缸蜗牛和一只难得一见的猫陪伴左右。雄心勃勃的编辑爱德华（爱尔登·埃伦瑞奇饰，Alden Ehrenreich）希望能改变这一现状，他作为最新一只从纽约远道而被送往宰杀的羔羊登场。他的任务不仅是让海史密斯再写一本新书（正如他后来所说，她的大多数作品都“很不稳定”），而是写另一部汤姆·雷普利（Tom Ripley）的故事。《天才雷普利》（The Talented Mr Ripley）依然是她最受喜爱的作品，他相信自己可以利用对她及其作品的崇拜，让她重新回到打字机前。", "links": [{"text": "It’s again based on a play", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/stage/2018/aug/09/switzerland-review-patricia-highsmith"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但海史密斯可不会听取一个“下属”的建议，也不会像其他许多作家那样变成一个“可供雇佣的妓女”。在发表了一系列反犹太和种族主义的言论（电影对她那些最恶劣的观点处理得有些轻描淡写）之后，她先是让他跳舞，最后才对他进行了考验：如果他能和她一起构思出一桩像样的谋杀案，她就会把雷普利带回来。我们进入了一部戏中戏，埃伦瑞奇饰演一个更加圆滑的美国人，在罗马对一位富有的女继承人（奥利维亚·库克饰，Olivia Cooke）进行围猎，这个角色是他根据在去见海史密斯的火车旅途中遇到的一位女性虚构出来的。在再次偶遇这位现实中的女性后，我们也跟随他展开了追求她的现实努力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是一个三线交织的故事，其结构让埃伦瑞奇成为了真正的男主角，而米伦在银幕外的时间比我们所希望的要多得多。由乔安娜·穆雷-史密斯（Joanna Murray-Smith）根据自己的话剧改编的剧本，并没有它自己想象的那般妙趣横生地恶毒，尤其是在试图展现海史密斯尖酸刻薄的极致时更是如此。她的世界观充满仇恨，但方式大体上显而易见（“快乐被高估了，”她像个情绪激动的青少年一样说道），我渴望看到更多尖锐的讽刺，然而影片只是触及了皮毛（当我们需要帕特里克·马伯（Patrick Marber）时，他却在哪里呢？）。米伦表现得妙趣横生，这标志着这位演员迎来了更具实质性的挑战——无论是为了凯特·温丝莱特（Kate Winslet）的儿子去死，还是与西莉亚·伊姆里（Celia Imrie）一起破解一桩轻而易举就能解开的谋杀案，她已经有很长一段时间没有接受过真正的考验了。这也是埃伦瑞奇的另一个绝佳机会，他早先试图成为好莱坞下一个当红炸子鸡的尝试失败了，但最终对他有利。他没有被困在《星球大战》（Star Wars）宇宙中或主演其他空洞的系列续作，而是顺应了自己邪魅俊朗的外表。他在《公平竞争》（Fair Play）中饰演一个傲慢的银行家、在《武器》（Weapons）中饰演一个酗酒的警察、在舞台剧《贝基·肖》（Becky Shaw）中饰演一个有毒性直率的单身汉，表现都非常出色。埃伦瑞奇既能轻松展现迷人魅力，又能将那种深不可测和令人不安的角色演得恰到好处，这无疑是对那部避无可避的《雷普利》重启版的一次极具说服力的试镜。", "links": [{"text": "dying for Kate Corbijn）自2015年的《生活》（Life）以来首次执导剧情片，他显然更擅长效仿意大利假雷普利那种光鲜亮丽的质感，而不是将海史密斯的家打造成一个充满舞台感、去氛围化地点之外的任何东西（诚然，奥利维亚·王尔德（Olivia Wilde）制作精良的晚宴喜剧《邀请函》（The Invite）最近刚把门槛拉高了），尽管这里有她的纪念品和武器库，但没有什么真正活过来。", "links": article_text:
T he restrictions of Covid led to an inevitable rise in safely contained chamber-piece movies, where a handful of characters find themselves in a usually remote house, dialogue taking obvious precedence over action. There were some highlights, such as Kevin Williamson’s timely slasher Sick , and some considerable low points, such as Sam Levinson’s vapid drama Malcolm & Marie , but while we had plenty of them, none of them rivalled some of the greatest and smartest pre-pandemic examples. The very best tended to be based on plays and quite often starred Michael Caine.

He was in Anthony Shaffer’s Sleuth, which went from Tony to Oscar success back in the 1970s, and then the arguably even better Deathtrap in the decade after, which Sidney Lumet adapted from Ira Levin’s deviously plotted play. In between there was also an under-seen TV movie called One of My Wives Is Missing , based on 60s play Trap for a Single Man, which was notably lesser but still delivered a similarly specific brand of twisty, talky thrills. There would be secrets, surprises, reversals and usually at least one dead body by the end of it, a subgenre entirely indebted to the work of Agatha Christie (who reportedly loved Sleuth on stage so much that she dedicated a picture of herself to be hung in the house used in the big screen adaptation). The bar is therefore held rather high, a puzzle that requires an ingenious level of writing that needs to be smart without smug and shocking without feeling cheap.

A Talent for Murder is an admirable, and rare, effort to bring that formula back, a biggish swing that almost lands. It’s again based on a play , and like both Sleuth and Deathtrap it’s based around a writer who weaves their way through a thriller plot of their own making. Standing in for Caine is Helen Mirren playing a fictionalised version of Patricia Highsmith, a famously cantankerous and bigoted author who hated to be around people and, like most misanthropes, preferred animals instead. We meet her in 1995 as she drinks herself to death in a remote Switzerland home, no more books to be written, a tank full of snails and a barely seen cat to keep her company. Ambitious editor Edward (Alden Ehrenreich) is hoping to change that, the latest lamb to be sent to the slaughter all the way from New York. He’s been tasked with getting Highsmith not just to write another new book (most of which have been “inconsistent”, as he later says) but, instead, another Tom Ripley caper. The Talented Mr Ripley remains her most beloved work, and he believes he can use his adoration of her and her work to get her back to the typewriter.

But Highsmith is not going to take the advice of an “underling” and won’t become a “hooker for hire” like so many other authors. In between making antisemitic and racist jabs (the film goes a little easy on her vilest of views), she makes him dance before finally putting him to the test: if he can help plot a worthy murder with her then she will bring Ripley back. We enter a film within a film as Ehrenreich plays a far more sleek American preying on a wealthy heiress (Olivia Cooke) in Rome, a character he concocts based on a woman he met on the train journey to meet Highsmith. After bumping into the real woman once again, we also follow his real efforts to romance her.

It’s three strands and the structure makes Ehrenreich the true lead with Mirren off-screen far more than we’d like. The script, adapted by Joanna Murray-Smith from her own play, isn’t quite as deliciously nasty as it seems to think it is, especially when trying to show Highsmith at her caustic worst. Her worldview is hateful but in ways more broadly obvious than not (“Happiness is overrated,” she says like an emo teen) and I craved for more cutting jabs, skin barely grazed (where is Patrick Marber when you need him?). Mirren is a hoot and it marks a more substantial challenge for the actor who, whether dying for Kate Winslet’s son or solving an easily solvable murder with Celia Imrie , hasn’t been put to the test for quite some time. It’s also another fantastic opportunity for Ehrenreich, whose earlier failed attempt to become Hollywood’s next best thing has ultimately worked out in his favour. Rather than being stuck in the Star Wars universe or leading other vacant franchise entries, he’s leaned into his sinister good looks. He was excellent as a bratty banker in Fair Play , an alcoholic cop in Weapons and a toxically direct bachelor on stage in Becky Shaw . Ehrenreich can easily charm while also playing unknowable and unsettling so well, a convincing enough audition for the unavoidable Ripley reboot.

The idea of the pair inventing a murder together is a fun one, with lines between fact and fiction blurring, but there’s not enough back-and-forth in these scenes as we watch the creation of a story far too generic to bear Highsmith’s name. We disappear into the fabricated world for too-long stretches without all that much at stake, and I wanted to see more of the process and how that affects what we then see. Director Anton Corbijn , making his first narrative film since 2015’s Life, is more comfortable trying to emulate the gloss of a fake Ripley in Italy than he is with turning Highsmith’s home into anything other than a stagey, atmosphere-free location (admittedly, Olivia Wilde’s gloriously well-crafted dinner party comedy The Invite recently raised the bar), and despite her memorabilia and armoury of weapons, nothing really comes alive.

We’re being led down a road of twists and turns but none really jolt or surprise as much as we expect, the rug never really being pulled, just gently tugged at. Mirren and Ehrenreich are a formidably talented duo, and I can’t imagine anyone else lifting this quite so well, but they’re not given anything truly vicious enough to work with. Knives are plunged, drinks are spiked and guns are fired but A Talent for Murder is lacking in real blood.

A Talent for Murder is premiering at the Toronto film festival and will be released in US cinemas on 23 October, in the UK on 20 November and in Australia on 26 December

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Hito Steyerl kritisiert die Unterwerfung der Kunst unter die Logik der Plattformen, eine Doku blickt auf das Imperium Larry Gagosians – und ein Essay fragt, warum Modeausstellungen so uninspiriert sind: Das ist unsere Medienschau am Montag"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kunstmarkt"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Daniel Grant erläutert im \"Observer\" , worauf Kunstsammler achten sollten, wenn sie Museen und Galerien Werke aus ausleihen möchten. Eine Ausstellung könne den Marktwert eines Kunstwerks steigern, weil sie dessen Qualität und kunsthistorische Bedeutung bestätige. Doch Leihverträge regelten weit mehr als Laufzeit und Transport: Auch Versicherung, Restaurierung, Urheberrechte und die Nennung des Besitzers müssten geklärt werden. article_text:
Hito Steyerl kritisiert die Unterwerfung der Kunst unter die Logik der Plattformen, eine Doku blickt auf das Imperium Larry Gagosians – und ein Essay fragt, warum Modeausstellungen so uninspiriert sind: Das ist unsere Medienschau am Montag

Kunstmarkt

Daniel Grant erläutert im "Observer" , worauf Kunstsammler achten sollten, wenn sie Museen und Galerien Werke aus ausleihen möchten. Eine Ausstellung könne den Marktwert eines Kunstwerks steigern, weil sie dessen Qualität und kunsthistorische Bedeutung bestätige. Doch Leihverträge regelten weit mehr als Laufzeit und Transport: Auch Versicherung, Restaurierung, Urheberrechte und die Nennung des Besitzers müssten geklärt werden. Besonders bei Auslandsleihen drohten Probleme durch ungeklärte Provenienzen oder Rückgabeforderungen. Bei kommerziellen Galerien sei zudem zwischen Leihe und Kommission zu unterscheiden: "Die Hauptaufgabe einer Galerie ist es, Kunst zu verkaufen; die eines Museums ist es, sie auszustellen." Sammler sollten deshalb vertraglich festhalten, dass ein Leihwerk nicht zum Verkauf steht. Auch die finanzielle Lage der Galerie zu prüfen, könne sich lohnen.

Maja Renfer beschreibt in "Ocula" die neue Messe Prospect Cologne als Teil eines Trends zu kleineren, experimentelleren Kunstmessen. Mit dem Format wolle man nicht mit der parallel stattfindenden Art Cologne konkurrieren, sagt Mitgründer Manoucher Khoshbakht. Vielmehr gehe es darum, eine Gemeinschaft aufzubauen. Mit dem Standort in der ehemaligen Staatlichen Hochschule für Fotografie wolle das Team zeigen, "dass das Rheinland wieder eine international interessante Szene ist". Für Monopol International hatte zuvor Kate Brown über die Prospect und andere kleine Messen berichtet.

James Marshall fragt in "Art Plugged" , ob ein Dokumentarfilm über Larry Gagosian das Imperium des einflussreichen Kunsthändlers ins Wanken bringen könnte. In "Shadow Man: Inside the Secret World of Larry Gagosian" nimmt der kanadische Regisseur Barry Avrich nach zwei Filmen über den Kunstmarkt und einen großen Fälschungsskandal nun Gagosian ins Visier. Der Film ist nicht autorisiert und soll laut Avrich weniger das Kunstgeschäft als vielmehr die Verbindung von Macht, Gier und Genie untersuchen. Im Zentrum stehe ein Mann, der die Kunstbranche geprägt, kontrolliert und manipuliert habe, um ein Galerieimperium aufzubauen – wenn nicht gar ein Monopol. Auch frühere Vorwürfe gegen die Galerie, darunter Anschuldigungen wegen Fehlverhaltens gegenüber Frauen und Berichte über Kontakte zu russischen Oligarchen, könnten eine Rolle spielen; ob der Film diese Themen aufgreift, ist jedoch offen. Ein Starttermin und Angaben zum Vertrieb stehen noch aus.

Kunst und Politik

Birgit Wittstock berichtet im "Standard" über das feministische Kunstwerk "Grüss Göttin" der Tiroler Künstlerin Ursula Beiler, das seit 2009 regelmäßig für politische Empörung sorgt. Zuletzt habe sich Niederösterreichs FPÖ-Chef Udo Landbauer an der Installation in St. Pölten gestört und ihre Entfernung gefordert: "Das ist nur mehr verrückt!" Beiler habe mit der gegenderten Grußformel ursprünglich das männliche Gottesbild hinterfragen und Frauen in der Tiroler Identität sichtbarer machen wollen. Das Schild sei seither wiederholt beschmiert, beschädigt und verändert worden. Schon 2019 hatte die FPÖ wegen einer Aufstellung in Innsbruck eine "Verletzung religiöser Gefühle" beklagt. Wittstock sieht in der Ausdauer der Empörung einen Beleg für die Wirksamkeit des Werks: Ein Standortwechsel genüge, um die Debatte nach 17 Jahren erneut zu entfachen.

Katrin Gottschalk und Sophie Jung sprechen in der "taz" mit Hito Steyerl über KI, politische Einflussnahme auf die Kunst und die eigene Rolle als Künstlerin . Den KI-Boom hält Steyerl für eine Blase: Ein Teil der geplanten Infrastruktur sei unnötig, Modelle ließen sich mit deutlich weniger Energie und Daten trainieren. Zugleich beschreibt sie ihre eigene Position als "kompliziert, auch kompromittiert", weil sie die Technologien kritisiere und zugleich Teil von ihnen sei. Mit Blick auf die Kulturpolitik warnt sie vor einem autoritären Klima und fordert mehr Autonomie für den Kunstbetrieb. Dieser sei inzwischen teilweise "wie ein Blinddarm sozialer Medien" und unterwerfe sich dem Aufmerksamkeitsprinzip der Plattformen. Auch den Kunstmarkt sieht sie kritisch: Hinter dem Glanz der Eröffnungen stünden Klassenunterschiede, Betrug und Ausbeutung. Anlass des Gesprächs ist Steyerls Werkschau "Deine Mudda macht Show" in den Hamburger Deichtorhallen.

Museen

Gabriella Angeleti fragt in "The Art Journal", warum Modeausstellungen in Museen so oft enttäuschend wirkten. Die Debatte um die abgesagte John-Galliano-Schau am Metropolitan Museum und eine Modenschau von Collina Strada im Storm King Art Center dienen ihr als Ausgangspunkt. Während die Präsentation von Gallianos Entwürfen an Schaufensterpuppen Fragen nach der Trennung von künstlerischer Leistung und persönlichem Fehlverhalten aufwerfe, hätten die Kleider bei Collina Stradas Laufstegshow durch die Bewegung der Körper eine ganz andere Wirkung entfaltet. Die Kunstwerke im Hintergrund seien dabei zur Kulisse geworden. Zugleich sei das Event von Kooperationen mit Möbel-, Getränke- und Zahnpflegemarken geprägt gewesen – ein unverhohlen kommerzielles Spektakel. Angeleti sieht darin einen grundsätzlichen Unterschied: Mode werde interessant, wenn sie getragen und bewegt werde. Im Museum dagegen stelle sich weniger die Frage, wer kuratieren dürfe, als vielmehr, was Kleidung jenseits ihres ursprünglichen Kontexts überhaupt ausmache.
